newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish banks' net doubles to PLN 4.1 bln in Q1-Q3.
newsitem.headline: Polish banks' net doubles to PLN 4.1 bln in Q1-Q3.

text.p: Polish banks' aggregate net profit doubled to 4.1 billion zlotys in the first three quarters of 1996 from two billion zlotys in the same period last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said on Wednesday.
It said in a report that the financial situation of banks improved mainly thanks to their consolidation and because their obligatory reserve requirements have been lowered.
The reserves totalled some 1.3 billion zlotys in the nine-month period, down from 2.1 billion last year.
GUS said that banks' gross profit in the January-September period rose to 5.8 billion from 3.2 billion last year while revenues increased by 23 percent to 25.3 billion zlotys.
It said gross and net profit margins increased to 22.9 percent and 16.3 percent respectively in the first nine months and banks with foreign capital showed the best improvement.
The margins were 15.6 percent and 9.9 percent respectively in the same period of 1995.
